title: A football game where the ball isn't glued to your feet - ProEvoClubs
author: ChrisLamaq
selftext:
Hi everyone!

I've been working on **ProEvoClubs**, an online 11v11 football (soccer) game for PC and Android. This is the first time I'm sharing it outside my own development environment, so I'm really curious to hear what you think.

The idea behind it is pretty simple: I missed the feeling that controlling the ball is actually a skill.

That's why the entire game is built around its own movement engine, **PEM (ProEvo Movement Engine)**, designed around one fundamental rule:  
**The ball is a free physics object. It isn't attached to the player. Nobody carries it. It only moves when a body part makes contact with it.**

Here's what that means in practice:

* **No magnetic first touch.** Your first touch depends on the ball's speed and height, your body angle, the part of your body you use, and whether a defender is putting pressure on you. Get it wrong, and the ball gets away from you.
* **Players have weight and inertia.** Every player has a center of mass. Changing direction requires braking, planting your foot and shifting your weight. You can't instantly turn 180 degrees while sprinting.
* **Physical contact is simulated, not played out through canned animations.** Shoulder-to-shoulder duels depend on mass, speed, posture and strength. Players stumble and recover based on their balance, and you can even trip over a player lying on the ground.
* **The ball follows real-world specifications.** It weighs 430 g, bounces 0.76 m when dropped from 2 m onto grass, shots fly between 70 and 121 km/h, and crosses and high shots curve with Magnus-effect spin.
* **Bots play by exactly the same rules.** The AI uses the same movement engine and can only perform the same actions available to human players. No hidden abilities, no perfect touches, no scripted advantages.

# Your club, your friends, one goal: promotion

Clubs are the heart of the game. Create one with your friends, play every match together and fight for promotion: seasons in 10-team divisions where the top 2 go up and the bottom 2 go down, all the way from the bottom tier to the first division. The more your club plays, the more its home ground grows.

# What's around the movement engine?

Some of the main features (I'll keep showing more here and on Discord):

* **Full football matches:** Referees, offside, cards, fouls, extra time and penalties. Goalkeepers can be controlled by humans or bots.
* **Player creator:** Create male and female players, customizing their bodies, faces, hairstyles, kits and boots.
* **Grounds and stadiums:** Every club starts with its own training ground (5 different starter designs, 2,000 seats each) that grows over time. There's also a 61,000-seat stadium with a full crowd, playable by day, at sunset, under cloudy skies or at night.
* **Online multiplayer:** Dedicated servers, with the goal of supporting full 11v11 matches with your friends. Bots fill empty positions, and if someone disconnects, a bot takes over until a substitute can come on.
* **Cross-platform:** PC (Steam) and Android cross-play, with native controller and keyboard support (touch controls coming later). The target is 60 FPS on mid-range phones.

It's still early in development: graphics, sound and menus are a work in progress, and right now I'm focused on animations and how it feels to play.

# Follow the development

* **Discord:** development updates, gameplay clips and, eventually, testers: [https://discord.gg/KVZgZdpAuY](https://discord.gg/KVZgZdpAuY)
* **Instagram:** [https://instagram.com/proevoclubs](https://instagram.com/proevoclubs)
* **Patreon:** if you'd like to support the project and get involved early: [https://www.patreon.com/c/ProEvoClubs](https://www.patreon.com/c/ProEvoClubs)
   * **Supporter (€5/month):** devlogs every 2 weeks, closed beta access, your name in the credits.
   * **Tester (€10/month):** everything above, plus alpha builds and testing sessions with me.
   * **Founder (€15/month):** everything above, plus an exclusive Founder kit (hoodie and pants) that will never be offered again.

# I'd really love your feedback!

* What made ball control feel good (or bad) for you in PES or FIFA/EA FC?
* In current football games, what's the one thing you'd most like to see fixed or improved?
